Published online:
    2 September 2026

Geographic focus:
    United States (North America)

Temporal focus:
    T1. Historical report [YES] — July 2026 factory orders data
    T2. Forward-looking reporting short-term risks (next few weeks/months) [YES] — ISM survey signals on August pricing, AI-driven capex momentum, supply chain strain from US-Israeli/Iran war
    T3. Forward-looking reporting long-term risks (next quarters/years) [IMPLICIT] — AI buildout as structural manufacturing tailwind, persistent war-related supply chain and input price pressures

Synopsis:
    US factory orders rose 0.9% MoM in July 2026, beating the 0.6% Reuters consensus, driven primarily by a 12.7% surge in civilian aircraft orders. Core capex orders (non-defense ex-aircraft) were flat, slightly below the preliminary +0.2% reading, though core capex shipments remained solid at +1.2%. Manufacturing is supported structurally by AI infrastructure spending but faces headwinds from elevated input prices tied to the ongoing US-Israeli war with Iran and import tariffs. The overall tone from ISM August data is cautious, with manufacturers flagging cost pressures.
